label: Heavy
summary: Too heavy for one person to move safely. Back injuries and crushed hands and feet are the most common salvage injuries, and without medical care they can end your ability to work.
signs: Anything over about 25 kg: appliances, batteries, motors, transformers, engines
Heavy for its size: transformers, lead-acid batteries, compressors, cast iron
Tall or top-heavy items like vending machines, shelving and fridges
Loads you can't see past or get a good grip on
do: Test the weight by tipping one corner before you commit
Strip off what you don't need and carry only the useful part
Use a second person, a hand truck, rollers, a pry bar or a ramp
Clear the path and decide where the load will go before you lift
Bend your knees, keep the load close and your back straight
Move your feet to turn; don't twist
dont: Don't lift heavy things when you're exhausted or rushing
Don't lift above shoulder height or reach out with a load
Don't carry heavy loads down stairs alone
Don't put fingers or feet under a load being lowered
Don't try to catch something that is falling: step away
firstAid: Free a trapped person as quickly as you safely can, then get medical help
Crushed fingers or toes: cool them, raise them, and check for a broken bone
Back strain: keep moving gently and stay as active as you can; avoid heavy lifting for a few days, but don't lie in bed, which slows recovery
Numb or weak legs, or loss of bladder or bowel control after a back injury, needs urgent medical care
Long crush injuries can damage the kidneys hours later, even if the person seems fine
